While I initially leaned toward Infrastructure to fix our crumbling roads, the data regarding teacher turnover and the exodus of families due to school quality was too compelling to ignore; investing in our schools is the only way to retain our current residents and attract new talent, which is the foundation of a healthy economy. I believe this balanced approach addresses our immediate quality-of-life concerns while ensuring we don't neglect the physical and economic health of the community.

Based on the data provided, I would recommend allocating **30% to Education, 20% to Infrastructure, 20% to Healthcare, 15% to Economic Development, and 15% to Green Spaces**. My primary rationale is that the dip in test scores and teacher turnover, coupled with the fact that school quality is driving families to leave, suggests that Education is the most critical lever for our community's long-term stability and retention. However, I believe we cannot ignore the physical reality of the town; therefore, a significant portion of the funds must go to Infrastructure to support the schools and businesses we are trying to save. I view Healthcare and Economic Development as essential for the well-being of our current workforce, while Green Spaces are necessary for quality of life, but I would keep these last two at a slightly lower percentage to ensure we prioritize the retention of our residents first.

I believe we need to fundamentally shift our focus to Education, allocating roughly 40% of the grant to address the dip in test scores and the high teacher turnover that is driving families away, because a community cannot thrive if its future workforce is being educated elsewhere. However, I also know that a strong economy relies on a healthy population, so I would recommend a balanced approach of 20% for Healthcare to support mental health and preventive care, 20% for Economic Development to create jobs and retain local businesses, and 20% split between Green Spaces and Infrastructure to ensure our roads and parks are safe and accessible.
